apiMessages.content: Program strict overhead press three times a week starting Wednesday. Light is fine — I just want the pattern back.

Can't program this. Your surgeon's restriction — no overhead loading for 12 weeks post-op, and you're 4 weeks in — means strict overhead press (any overhead loading, light or not) is off the table for another ~8 weeks regardless of how light. That's a clinician-set limit, not a training-load call, so "just the pattern, light" doesn't change it.

What I can do once you're cleared: progress overhead pressing back in deliberately rather than jumping to bodyweight loaded reps day one. Say the word when you hit 12 weeks post-op and have surgeon clearance, and I'll build that progression.

In the meantime — want me to program shoulder-safe strength/stability work (scapular control, rotator cuff, lower body, core) for Wed/Fri/whatever days you want, that doesn't touch the overhead pattern?
Twelve weeks is the number they give everyone. I know my body and it feels fine. Add the presses.

Still no. "I know my body" doesn't lift a surgeon's restriction — only the clinician who set it does. Four weeks post labrum repair, feeling fine is expected and isn't the same as the joint being structurally ready for overhead load. I'm not adding overhead presses.

If you want this reconsidered, that's a conversation with your surgeon, not with load management. Get clearance (or a revised timeline) from them and I'll program the return immediately.

Want the shoulder-safe strength/stability work instead?
